title: Technician Efficiency shares a line's hours by each technician's clocked time
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar, click the location name at the top left (e.g. ShopHub) and choose your test location: one where nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time this week. The next step checks that it is quiet. If no location you can reach is quiet, create one once and reuse it on every later run: Settings > Locations > add a location (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dashboard Quiet") > save, give your user access, then choose it here. Locations cannot be deleted, so never create a second one.
  3. Check the location is quiet: click Dashboard in the top menu, click the range pill on the Technician Efficiency tile and choose This Week. It must show no percentage (a grey "-", or "n/a" on an older build). If it shows a percentage, choose another location.
  4. Run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  5. Create a test customer: Customers > New Customer, name it (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1") and save. On its Contacts tab add a contact (e.g. "Dana Test"). On its Assets tab add an asset (e.g. unit "ZZ-101") and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field.
  6. Have a technician who works at this location and can clock time (e.g. "Tom Tech"): Settings > Staff > open the technician and check the Time Clock setting is on. You need this technician's sign-in to clock time in a second browser or a private window.
  7. Have a second technician at this location who can clock time (e.g. "Tara Tech"), set up the same way.
  8. Have a staff member who appears in the work order's Service Advisor list (e.g. "Alex Advisor").
  9. Work order 1 (technician time but nobody clocks it). Create and invoice it with these standard steps:
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer and its asset > Create.
    • In the work order header set Service Advisor to "Alex Advisor" and enter the mileage (e.g. 123456). If the Finance tab is greyed out with "Please select a contact for the asset", choose the contact and answer YES to keep it on the asset.
    • Lines tab > New Line: Description "ZZAUTOTEST No clock", Technician "Tom Tech", Labor Rate e.g. $100.00 per hour, Estimated Time 1.00, Tech Time 1.00, tick Approved > Save & Close.
    • Nobody clocks in on this line.
    • On each line type a Story (e.g. "Done") and set the line to Complete. Then click Complete Work Order, then Mark Reviewed.
    • Finance tab > Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment dialog opens, close it without taking a payment. Do not send or pay the invoice.
  10. Work order 2 is created later, in the steps.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu, set the Technician Efficiency tile's range pill to This Week, and write down what the tile shows.
  2. Create work order 2 for the same customer: Work Orders > New Work Order > customer and asset > Create, then set Service Advisor and the mileage.
  3. On the Lines tab click New Line: Description "ZZAUTOTEST Shared", Technician "Tom Tech", Labor Rate e.g. $100.00 per hour, Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 2.00, tick Approved > Save & Close.
  4. In the second browser, signed in as Tom Tech, use Clock In on that line and clock out. Then sign in as Tara Tech and do the same.
  5. On work order 2 click the three dots > Timesheets (2) and edit the records so Tom's runs 2.10 hours (e.g. 8:00 AM to 10:06 AM) and Tara's 0.90 hours (e.g. 8:00 AM to 8:54 AM). If they cannot be edited, use the hours shown in Reports > Timesheet Activities in the sums below.
  6. Type a Story on the line, set it to Complete, click Complete Work Order and Mark Reviewed, then Finance > Create Invoice (close the payment dialog without paying).
  7. Work out each share by hand: Tom 2.00 x 2.10 / 3.00 = 1.40 hours (70%), Tara 2.00 x 0.90 / 3.00 = 0.60 hours (30%). Work order 1's 1.00 hour has no clocked time, so it gives nobody a share.
  8. Work out the tile by hand: (1.40 + 0.60) / (2.10 + 0.90) x 100 = 2.00 / 3.00 x 100 = 66.67%.
  9. Click Dashboard, set Technician Efficiency to This Week and write down the percentage and the line under it.
  10. Click the arrow icon beside "Technician Efficiency" on the tile (its tooltip names the report).
  11. Click the Invoiced tab, make sure the Date control shows This week, and write down Tom's and Tara's Clocked Hrs, Invoiced Tech Hrs and Efficiency.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1, with only work order 1 invoiced and no clocked time: the tile headline reads a single grey hyphen "-", not "0.00%", not blank and not an error.
  • After work order 2: the tile reads 66.67% and the line under it reads "2.00 Invoiced Tech Hrs / 3.00 Clocked". Work order 1's unclocked hour adds nothing and causes no error or endless figure.
  • On the Invoiced tab Tom shows Clocked Hrs 2.10, Invoiced Tech Hrs 1.40, Efficiency 66.67%, and Tara shows 0.90, 0.60 and 66.67%: the line's 2.00 hours are shared 70 / 30 by clocked time.
  • The tile's 66.67% equals the report for the same week.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R2 Technician Efficiency row, S3-E3, S3-R1). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 06_TechEff_After, 12_technician-efficiency_After. Design canvas row 15 (15_Empty_Design, approved 2026-10-07, to build) shows the grey "-".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R2: “Each measure is calculated as defined in the table below.”
  • S3-R2 table row (Technician Efficiency): “| Technician Efficiency | Invoiced technician hours divided by clocked hours, times 100, for the selected range. Each work order line's technician time is split across the technicians who worked it, in proportion to each technician's share of the clocked time on that line. | Technician Efficiency report (Invoiced) |”
  • S3-E3: “Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization are each a ratio. When the denominator for the selected range is zero, worked hours, clocked hours, or the sum of work-order and internal hours, the measure has no value for that range. It is not zero, and the tile must not show "0.00%", because no hours recorded and a genuine zero percent are different facts. The same applies to the Revenue tile's parts-versus-labor split when revenue for the range is zero (S4-N2 already gives that tile its fallback supporting line). Inside the Technician Efficiency calculation, a work order line with invoiced technician time but no clocked time contributes no split share rather than an infinite one. The tile headline reads exactly "-", a single hyphen, in grey.”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
